title: Humble in prayer
hookLine: successful are the believers who are humble in their prayer and turn from idle talk (23:1–3)

cards: A man walks into the mosque in Medina, prays quickly, and comes over to greet the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet returns his greeting and says: go back and pray, for you have not prayed.
The man prays again the same way, and returns. Go back and pray; you have not prayed. A third time.
Finally the man says: by the One who sent you with the truth, I don't know how to do it better. Teach me. Bukhari records what he was told.
Today, a new surah, Al-Mu'minun, the Believers.

teach.h: SUCCESSFUL ARE THE HUMBLE IN PRAYER.
teach.b: The surah opens with a promise. Pickthall: "Successful indeed are the believers who are humble in their prayers". Among the first things named next is turning away from idle talk.
Humble in their prayers is khashi'un, people with khushu'. It's a hard word to put in English.
The Qur'an uses the same root for land lying still and lowly, waiting for rain, and for voices gone hushed before God on the Last Day. So khushu' isn't only a feeling of humility.
It's a stillness, a settling, where the noise goes down and attention gathers. The man in the mosque wasn't lazy or rude. He was going fast.
And the Prophet's teaching to him, in Bukhari's account, was mostly about time.

teach.h: BOW UNTIL YOU ARE AT REST.
teach.b: Bow until you are at rest in your bowing. Rise until you're standing straight. Prostrate until you are at rest in prostration.
Sit until you're at rest sitting. At rest, again and again. Not more words, not harder feelings: slower bodies.
That's why the next line of the surah fits: turning from idle talk. Khushu' is hard to reach with a phone buzzing in your pocket and half a conversation still running in your head.
The hurried man got three chances and then a lesson, not a scolding. Khushu' isn't a test you pass once. It's a place you return to, one position at a time.

how: In the five daily prayers, Muslims are taught to pause at rest in each position, called tuma'nina, and teachers speak of khushu' as the inner stillness the outward rest is meant to support.

o: stillness in prayer, where attention gathers
a long list of words recited after prayer
a loud, tearful voice raised during prayer

p: said three times to a hurried man
how to bow, rise and prostrate

s: the hurried man was scolded for skipping prayer
he did pray. he was told to go back because he rushed it.
the root of khushu' is also used for still, lowly land
the Qur'an uses it for earth lying lowly, waiting for rain, and for hushed voices.
in the hadith, the hurried man was sent back only once
he was sent back three times before he asked to be taught.

games.q: you've been sent back to pray three times. you finally say: teach me. what are you taught?
o: to rest in each position before moving on.
to pray in a quieter corner.
games.why: bow until at rest, rise until straight, prostrate until at rest. the lesson was about time.

practice: If you pray, take the next prayer you're due to pray, and let every position come to rest before you move to the next.
If you don't, do one ordinary thing that way right now: stand slowly, sit slowly, take one breath all the way to the end. Let each part finish before the next begins.

wordCard.voice: Khushu'. Humility in prayer, a stillness where attention gathers, like land lying quiet before rain. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: khushu', humility and stillness in prayer; 23:2 calls the believers khashi'un.

carryVoice: Your line: not more words, slower bodies. Stillness is a place to return to. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: Successful indeed are the believers who are humble in their prayers

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 757 (the man who prayed hurriedly)
